events.description: 35. MINUTE ENTRY and ORDER (AGS): On May 16, 2025, the Court held a motion hearing. For the reasons set out on the record, the motions to intervene (ECF 6, 7, 8 ) are granted in part. The proposed intervenors are permitted to intervene as of right. Otherwise, the motions are denied as moot. By May 30, 2025, the parties must meet and confer and contact the Court with a proposed motion schedule for the anticipated motions to dismiss and preliminary-injunction motion. Any motion to dismiss in this case must address the standing and ripeness issues discussed at todays hearing. All responsive pleading deadlines are vacated pending the parties new schedule. (Court Reporter/ECR James Pence). (Plaintiff Attorney: Eric W. Lee) (Defense Attorneys: Julia A. Gomez, Curtis Lee Morrison, Jennifer E. Rosenberg (remotely), Ari J. Savitzky, William Kyle Hancock, Lalitha D. Madduri) (no document attached) (lrc) (Entered: 05/16/2025)

events.description: 42. ORDER (AGS): The parties' almost fully joint motion to stay (ECF 39 ) is granted. The Court has considered defendant League of Women Voters' arguments, but still believes that the Supreme Court's upcoming decision in Bost will likely control the standing question here. As a result, and given how actively Bost is being litigated, the Court concludes it is in the best interests of justice to stay this case until the Court receives the Supreme Court's guidance. Within seven days of the resolution of Bost by the Supreme Court, the parties must file a motion to lift the stay and provide a recommended case management schedule going forward. Signed by District Judge Andrew G. Schopler on 07/30/2025.(no document attached) (mxa) (Entered: 07/30/2025)
